mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% indicates a tight labor market, which typically leads to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when UNRATE is below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand and business investment, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS increase.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates a contraction in the manufacturing sector, leading to expectations of reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when INDPRO is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly real GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 2.0% signals robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a strong labor market and robust consumer spending, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when both PAYEMS and RSAFS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5%.
